=== DETERMINISM ===
PASS. grep for utc_now/DateTime.now/:os.system_time/System.system_time/:rand/:random/Enum.random/Process.sleep/:timer.sleep across both test files matches only the two COMMENTS that say 'never DateTime.utc_now/0'. The one real-clock value touched is asserted only for shape (`%Registration{migrations_applied_at: %NaiveDateTime{}}` at migrations_test.exs:230), never for a value. Uniqueness comes from Ecto.UUID.generate/0 (never compared against a fixed expectation) and System.unique_integer([:positive, :monotonic]) (a VM counter, not an RNG) -- the same two mechanisms identity_test.exs and tenant_provisioning_test.exs already use. No hand-rolled seed anywhere. The §4 guard test's probe versions derive from the same VM counter, not from a clock or an RNG.

=== ASYNC SAFETY (ISS-0011 judgement) ===
PASS -- the split is correct, and no new instance of ISS-0011's pattern was introduced.
Re-derived from the actual `use` lines, not from the moduledoc prose: schemas_test.exs:24 is `use ExUnit.Case, async: true`; migrations_test.exs:29 is `use Letflow.DataCase, async: false`.
- schemas_test.exs async: true is SAFE. It does not use Letflow.DataCase (no connection is checked out), issues zero Repo calls, and grep for telemetry/Application.put_env/:persistent_term/Agent/GenServer/:global/Process.register/System.put_env/start_supervised/Registry across it returns no match (the only 'telemetry' hit is its own moduledoc sentence saying it attaches none, and the only 'global' hits are the :global_seq FIELD name). It touches nothing global or cross-process -- it reads compiled module metadata via __info__/1, __schema__/1, Ecto.Enum.values/2 and Code.fetch_docs/1, and builds changesets in-process. ISS-0011's root cause (a process-wide :telemetry.attach/4 on [:letflow, :repo, :query] inside an async: true module) is structurally unreachable here: a module that issues no query cannot receive its own event, and it subscribes to nothing. Confirmed the only :telemetry.attach call sites in the whole test tree remain test/letflow/plugs/tenant_status_test.exs:127 and :148 -- REQ-021's pre-existing ones. No new instance.
- migrations_test.exs async: false is CORRECT and NECESSARY. It switches Letflow.Repo to Sandbox :auto mode (:192 and :443) because Ecto.Migrator genuinely needs a second connection beyond DataCase's checked-out one; :auto mode checks in existing connections pool-wide, so it must not run alongside anything else. ExUnit drains all async modules before any sync module and runs sync modules one at a time, so there is no other connection to disturb. This mirrors test/letflow/tenant_provisioning_test.exs's already-established, already-reviewed precedent (:345, :396) exactly.

=== CLEANUP / ORPHAN CHECK ===
PASS, and verified in the harder failure path, not just the happy path.
Baseline letflow_test2 before any of my runs: 8 public tables, 13 schema_migrations versions, 0 tenant_% schemas, 0 tenants rows, 0 tenant_schemas rows, 0 event-store tables in public.
After the mutation-1 runs -- during which the mutated migration genuinely DID create a stray public.instance_sequence and the guard test FAILED -- the on_exit defensive cleanup at migrations_test.exs:458-473 still ran and dropped it: public tables back to the same 8, probe versions gone from public.schema_migrations, 0 tenant_% schemas, 0 orphan rows. That is the important result: the cleanup was exercised in the failure case (on_exit runs after a failed test too), which is the case that actually matters for a shared database.
Final state after all work, re-queried directly against letflow_test2:
  tenant_% schemas               = 0
  public tables                  = 8 (identical to baseline)
  schema_migrations rows         = 13 (identical to baseline)
  stray sub-timestamp versions   = 0 (no leftover 99x_xxx_xxx probe versions)
  tenants rows / tenant_schemas rows = 0 / 0
  event-store tables in public   = 0
The cleanup design is also safe by construction: the §4 block's stray-drop only fires for a name in the six-table map AND absent from the pre-test snapshot, so it can never destroy pre-existing state. Every :auto-mode describe block registers its on_exit before the work it needs to undo.

=== SPEC-vs-CODE CROSS-CHECK ===
All 20 cases the spec lists map to a real, named, executing test; the spec's coverage table (AC1 -> 1,2,3; AC2 -> 4,5; AC3 -> 6,7,8,9; AC4 -> 10,11,12,13,14; AC5 -> 15,16,17; plus carry-forwards 18,19,20) matches the code. The REQ-022 refresh in commit c18de8c is accurate and REMOVES NO COVERAGE -- it only updates two stale present-tense 'tenant_scoped_migrations/0 returns [] today' statements to past tense and adds a cross-reference; the REQ-022 fixture-based guard test is explicitly retained, deliberately outside the production manifest, so REQ-022's own coverage stays independent of what the manifest later contains.

No check failed. Verdict: PASS. Four non-blocking MINOR observations recorded below; none of them is a gate failure and none is re-filing ISS-0012..ISS-0020.

issues.title: Two guard-probe version constants live in two files with no shared source
